# Manato Fujimoto（藤本まなと）

> Manato Fujimoto（藤本まなと） is an Associate Professor (Ph.D. in Engineering) at the Graduate School of Informatics, Osaka Metropolitan University（大阪公立大学 大学院情報学研究科）, Japan, and a member of the Smart Platform Research Group（スマートプラットフォーム研究室）. Research areas: Ubiquitous Computing, Wireless Sensing, Activity Recognition, Healthcare & Well-being（ユビキタスコンピューティング、無線センシング、行動認識、ヘルスケア・ウェルビーイング）.

This is the official personal website of Manato Fujimoto. Last updated: 2026-11-06.

## About

I am an associate professor in the Graduate School of Informatics at Osaka Metropolitan University and a member of the Smart Platform Research Group. My research spans ubiquitous computing, wireless networks, sensing technologies, and elderly monitoring. I received my B.E., M.E., and Ph.D. in Engineering from Kansai University in 2009, 2011, and 2015. Before joining Osaka Metropolitan University in 2022, I worked at Nara Institute of Science and Technology and Osaka City University. I was also a visiting scientist at RIKEN's Center for Advanced Intelligence Project (AIP) from May 2018 to March 2026.

## Research

Connecting sensing, machine learning, and real-world applications to understand people and their environments.

### Sensing for Care & Healthy Aging

We study ways to recognize the daily activities of older adults and the work of caregivers. By bringing together activity logs and measurements of physical or psychological state, we aim to support care reporting and a better understanding of caregiver workload.

Topics: BLE-based activity logging, caregiver stress analysis, and sensor-based walking and exercise support.

### Human Activity & State Recognition

We combine wearable and environmental sensors to capture everyday behavior. Our work includes SipSense for beverage type and volume estimation, FocusSense for concentration estimation, and device-free recognition of activities in living spaces.

Topics: Acoustic sensing, multimodal concentration estimation, Doppler sensing, and daily activity recognition.

### Smart Spaces & Cities

We explore how everyday spaces can sense people and support their activities. Research ranges from turning ordinary furniture into touch interfaces to wireless crowd sensing and participatory sensing for tourism.

Topics: Vibration-based interfaces, Wi-Fi sensing, participatory sensing, and context-aware services.

### Wireless Localization & In-body Systems

We investigate localization and wireless communication for devices in challenging environments, including the human body. This work combines wireless and magnetic-field measurements with machine learning to support future medical and healthcare systems.

Topics: Magnetic-field-based localization, implant communications, UWB, and RFID localization.
